name: ProductPackageDetail
intent: Route-injectable product package surface: identity, version, dependencies, outputs, permission gates, evidence and install state, over a governed install — a plan, a confirmation dialog, and a success receipt carrying package, version, project and actor. It owns no shell and no router, so it mounts inside a workspace route that already has a sidebar and a top bar.
when: A product / package detail drill-in inside a Connect product centre
Any surface where installing something needs a plan, a confirmation and a receipt
A catalogue entry read by both viewers and installers
whenNot: Browsing many packages at once -> use AppMarketplace or DataTable
A four-step install with a planner, release evidence capture and blocker codes -> use InstallProductDialog
A generic record drill-in with no install -> use RecordDetailShell

chooseOver.component: Card + Dialog + Badge + Button composed at the application layer
chooseOver.because: That is what the Connect prototype did, and it duplicated product-package composition — sections, gate rendering, the install plan, the confirmation and the receipt — in application state. This owns the package surface while leaving the shell, the route and the authorisation decision with the host.

package.note: id, name, version; optional apiName, description, publisher, kind, channel, publishedAt, details.

outputs.note: What the install writes: add | replace | link.

permissions.note: The role gates, each with whether the acting user satisfies it.

installState.note: not-installed | installed | outdated | installing | failed, with the installed version.

target.note: Where an install lands. Without it the action has nothing to act on.

canInstall.note: The host's authorisation answer. False disables the install action and nothing else.

denialReason.note: State the refusal — a greyed button is not an explanation.

blockers.note: Refusals from the host's planner. Listed on the plan; they close the confirm.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Dependency, output, permission and evidence ids must be unique within their list.

headerActions.description: Extra identity-header actions — View in catalogue, Copy manifest

footer.description: Rendered under the sections, in the same column

states.outdated: The action names the upgrade — Upgrade to <version>.
states.installed: The action is parked once the installed version is the current one.
states.installing: Pending while the host's apply settles.
states.failed: The failure is stated; nothing claims to have installed.
states.unauthorized: Only the install action is disabled, with the denial reason stated under it.
states.blocked: Planner refusals are listed on the page and on the plan, and the confirm is closed.

allowedPlacement: inside a route that already owns its shell (CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar, or a WC3 workspace slot)
forbiddenPlacement: as a page that supplies its own sidebar, top bar or routing
inside a dialog — the install confirmation is already a dialog
evaluationCriteria: An unauthorized persona still reads every section; only the install action is disabled.
The refusal is stated in words, not implied by a disabled control.
Nothing is written before the confirmation: onInstall runs on confirm, and the receipt only after it settles.
The host owns the shell and the route; the widget renders neither.
At 820px the install panel stacks under the package rather than beside it.

lineage.authoredBy: Core #206 — the injectable package surface the Connect Product Center needed (2026-09-09)

derivedFrom.source: The Connect Core prototype's ProductDetail, which composed Card + Dialog + Badge + Button and held the install receipt in application state
extracted: compact identity header with kind, version and channel
dependencies, outputs, permissions, evidence and version sections
disabled/read-only presentation with an explicit denial reason
success receipt carrying package, version, project and actor

notes: Authorisation is an input, never a decision the widget makes: it renders canInstall and denialReason, and touches nothing else on the surface.
Blockers are shown but never hidden behind the action — the plan stays reachable so a viewer can see WHY, and only the confirm is closed.
onInstall may return a promise; the action holds its pending state until it settles, and the receipt is stamped only after it resolves.
It is not InstallProductDialog: that is the four-step planner-driven flow over the WC3 fixture types, this is the package surface with a single governed confirmation over product-neutral props.

usage: Use ProductPackageDetail to enhance your user interface. This component provides a consistent, accessible, and well-designed solution for this use case.
ProductPackageDetail integrates seamlessly with other components in the design system. Follow the established patterns and guidelines to ensure consistency across your application.

props.name: package
props.description: The package this surface is about.

props.name: installState
props.description: What the target project already has. Omit it and the package reads as not installed.

props.name: target
props.description: Where an install would land. Without it the install action has nothing to act on and is hidden.

props.name: actor
props.description: Who is acting. Named on the confirmation and carried on the receipt.

props.name: canInstall
props.description: Whether this persona may install. False disables the install action  and nothing else  — the package's details stay readable, because a viewer still has to be able to read them.

props.name: denialReason
props.description: Why the action is refused. Required in spirit whenever `canInstall` is false: state the reason.

props.name: blockers
props.description: Refusals from the host's planner. They are listed on the plan and they stop the confirm.

props.name: installLabel
props.description: Overrides the derived action label ("Install", "Upgrade to 2.1.0", "Installed").

props.name: headerActions
props.description: Extra actions for the identity header — "View in catalogue", "Copy manifest".

props.name: footer
props.description: Rendered under the sections, inside the same column.

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
